Description: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous for its floating phumdis (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, and organic matter) and serves as a lifeline for the local fishing community. The lake hosts the only floating national park in the world.

Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous for its floating phumdis (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, and organic matter) and serves as a lifeline for the local fishing community. The lake hosts the only floating national park in the world.

World's only floating national park located on Loktak Lake. It is the last natural refuge of the endangered Sangai deer (brow-antlered deer), which gracefully walks on the floating biomass. The park is a biodiversity hotspot.
Address: Near Loktak Lake, Bishnupur District, Manipur

Description: Historical embodiment of Manipur's power till 1891. The fort complex contains ancient temples, royal palaces, a moat, and two towering gateways. It serves as a symbol of Manipuri identity and is surrounded by lush gardens.

Historical embodiment of Manipur's power till 1891. The fort complex contains ancient temples, royal palaces, a moat, and two towering gateways. It serves as a symbol of Manipuri identity and is surrounded by lush gardens.

Historic Vaishnavite centre featuring twin golden domes and a paved courtyard. The temple houses shrines of Lord Krishna, Balaram, and Jagannath. It attracts thousands of devotees during Rath Yatra festival.
Asia's largest all-women market run by over 3,000 'Imas' (mothers). They sell fresh vegetables, fruits, handmade textiles, and traditional household goods. It is a vibrant cultural landmark.

An anthropological museum with rich collections of tribal heritage, portraits of former rulers, traditional costumes, arms, and ancient manuscripts. The museum also displays rare coins and musical instruments.
Address: Near Polo Ground, Imphal West, Manipur

Description: Commemorates the British and Indian soldiers who died during World War II. Managed by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, it features perfectly maintained stone markers and bronze plaques.
Home to the rare Sangai deer and various endangered species like the Himalayan black bear and python. Located at the foot of pine-growing hillocks, it offers a pleasant escape into nature.
Address: Iroisemba, Imphal-Kangchup Road, Imphal West, Manipur

Description: Small aesthetically pleasing lake surrounded by green foliage-rich hillocks. Offers boating facilities and a tranquil environment for picnics. The view of the sunset over the hills is spectacular.
Covers 200 acres with over 110 rare varieties of orchids, including dozens of endemic species. The peak blooming season is March-April when the entire garden bursts into vibrant colours.
Address: National Highway No. 39, Imphal West, Manipur

Description: A 15th-century Vishnu temple built of small bricks with Chinese architectural influence during King Kiyamba's reign. The temple is a protected monument and the town is also known for chiselled stoneware.
A hillock where British and Japanese forces fought a fierce battle during World War II. Features the 'India Peace Memorial' monument honouring the Japanese soldiers who died there.
Tall minar commemorating the Meitei and tribal martyrs who sacrificed their lives fighting the British in 1891. Located in Bir Tikendrajit Park, it is a prominent landmark in the city.
Address: Bir Tikendrajit Park, Imphal West, Manipur

Description: An island located on Loktak Lake offering panoramic views of the lake and floating phumdis. Popular for boating and photography. The island provides a unique vantage point to observe the floating vegetation.
A quaint town where Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and the Indian National Army fought the British. It is known for the INA Memorial and its serene lakeside location.
World's tallest mud dam offering scenic views of rice paddies and green hills. The peaceful reservoir behind the dam is ideal for picnics and nature walks.
Memorial dedicated to the Indian National Army and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. The complex features a bronze statue of Netaji and a museum displaying INA relics and historical photographs.
Ancient cave system with complex tunnels, five exits, and 34 junctions featuring beautiful stalactite and stalagmite formations. Popular among trekkers and adventure enthusiasts.
Hidden eco-tourism spot with crystal-clear water, green valleys, and designated picnic areas. The park is well-maintained and perfect for a relaxing family getaway.
Cultural complex housing pottery, rare coins, manuscripts, paintings, and replicas of traditional tribal houses. It provides deep insights into Manipur's artistic heritage.
Home to the rare Shirui lily (state flower of Manipur) found only in the Shirui Hill Range. The park also houses diverse bird species and small mammals.
Scenic hill range famous for the rare Shirui lily and panoramic views of Ukhrul's rolling landscapes. The hills offer moderate trekking opportunities and breathtaking sunrises.
Beautiful valley known for Dzukou lilies and pristine green landscapes. Popular among trekkers for its gentle slopes and spectacular views of the surrounding mountains.
Scenic waterfall near Loktak Lake. The water cascades down from a moderate height into a clear pool, making it a popular spot for photography and picnics.
Ancient village with historical ruins and remnants of old fortifications. It holds archaeological significance, offering glimpses into Manipur's pre-colonial history.
Memorial commemorating the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891. The site features a tall pillar and statues of Manipuri warriors who fought against the British.
Traditional village known for its pottery and unique cultural practices. Visitors can observe traditional Manipuri potters at work and explore the Mutua Museum nearby.
Serene and lesser-visited public park in Kakching district. It is well-maintained with flowering plants, walking paths, and seating areas ideal for a peaceful retreat.
Picturesque town on the Indo-Myanmar border. Known for its bustling border market, cross-cultural trade, and as a gateway to Southeast Asia.
Hidden gem with dense forests, big waterfalls, and abundant birdlife. Known for deep gorges, orange orchards, and the Zeilad Lake.
Cascading waterfalls that fall in steps forming small natural pools. The area is surrounded by thick forests and is a beautiful spot for nature lovers.
Lake famous for its variety of fishes, birds, and pythons. The pristine water and surrounding hills make it an ideal spot for birdwatching.
The highest hill station of Manipur. Known for scenic landscapes, the rare Shirui lily, and adventure trekking opportunities along the hill ridges.
A nature lover's paradise with preserved natural beauty. The district is known for its moderate climate and picturesque villages.
Town on Tiddim Road known for its vibrant tribal culture and scenic surroundings. It is the headquarters of Churachandpur district.
Scenic waterfall near Imphal. Surrounded by lush greenery, it is a popular weekend picnic destination for locals.
Beautiful waterfall located in the Imphal region. The water cascades down a rocky terrain, creating a serene environment.
Scenic waterfall near Kanglatongbi. The spot is surrounded by green hills and is popular among nature enthusiasts.
Breathtaking hilltop with panoramic views of Ukhrul's rolling landscapes. Ideal for camping, trekking, and stargazing away from city lights.
Natural limestone cave in Ukhrul featuring large chambers and interesting rock formations. Adventure seekers enjoy exploring its dark interiors.
Scenic spot in Ukhrul known for its natural beauty and tranquillity. Offers pristine views of the surrounding valleys and forests.
Open natural site with no entry fee. Recommended to visit early morning for the best sunrise experience.
Public residential and agricultural area known for eco-tourism and cultural heritage. Visitors can experience rural Manipuri life.
Traditional village where it is customary to offer a small donation to the village headman. The village is known for its preserved ancient customs.
Historic polo ground where Manipur, the birthplace of modern polo, is celebrated. The ground is located in the heart of Imphal.
A major sports stadium in Imphal hosting various sporting events and athletic meets.
A park and resort offering scenic views and recreational activities including boating and children's play areas.
Biodiversity park in Jiribam known for its rich flora and fauna. It serves as a conservation area for native plant species.
Memorial commemorating the Nupi Lal (Women's War) of 1939, where Manipuri women protested against British policies. An important historical monument.
Popular picnic spot with scenic views and recreational facilities. The area is well-shaded and perfect for family outings.
Scenic waterfall in Churachandpur popular among nature lovers. The waterfall is surrounded by dense forests.
Garden in Lamlai offering scenic views and recreational facilities. Known for its well-maintained lawns.
Old village built on a steep hill. A unique historical site for travellers interested in traditional architecture and tribal history.
Traditional village in Senapati known for its cultural heritage and the presence of ancient megalithic stones.
Traditional village known for its unique cultural practices and the famous Makhel stone monoliths.
Scenic meadow in Tamenglong popular for picnics and nature walks. The grassland is surrounded by dense woods.
District known for its cultural heritage and scenic landscapes. The region is famous for the Khongjom War Memorial.
District known for its tribal culture and natural beauty. The terrain is hilly and covered with thick forests.
District bordering Cachar District of Assam. Known for its railhead and scenic beauty, it acts as a gateway to Manipur.
Ancient temple dedicated to the Manipuri god Marjing. Located on a hilltop, it offers a panoramic view of the Imphal valley.
Temple located on Kaina Hill. Legend says it was visited by Shri Gouranga. Offers a spiritual retreat with scenic views.
Important pre-Hindu deity temple dedicated to Thangjing, the protector god of Moirang. Rich in cultural traditions.
A picturesque lake near Ningthoukhong village. It supports local fishing and is a habitat for migratory birds.
One of the largest lakes in Manipur, known for its natural beauty and rich aquatic biodiversity.
Beautiful lake surrounded by hills and agricultural fields. It provides irrigation to the surrounding farmlands.
A scenic lake located near the foothills. It is less crowded and perfect for a quiet day out.
A hidden waterfall deep within the Ukhrul forests. The trek to the waterfall is rewarding with pristine waters.
A majestic waterfall in Tamenglong known for its thunderous sound and picturesque surroundings.
A modest hill located near the orchidarium, offering easy hiking trails and views of the Imphal basin.
A small hill town known for its pristine environment and tribal heritage. It offers a glimpse into the traditional Naga lifestyle.
